real-time bidding. We should offer a global setting (default OFF) in Shields which would:\r\n\r\n1. Automatically deny all data sharing (like the option that's available in the Cliqz browser and can be verified using the [re:consent extension](https://chrome.google.com/webstore/detail/reconsent/djcdlbbfldmndgenehaifaiiahhhagfa)) in first-party consent manager platforms which follow the [IAB protocol](https://github.com/InteractiveAdvertisingBureau/GDPR-Transparency-and-Consent-Framework/blob/master/TCFv2/TCF-Implementation-Guidelines.md).\r\n2. Hide banners using the [Easylist-Cookie](https://easylist-downloads.adblockplus.org/easylist-cookie.txt) cosmetic filters.\r\n\r\nWe could surface that setting the first time a user encounters a cookie banner via a notification.\r\n\r\nAlternatively, instead of a new global setting, we could tie this feature to the existing \"aggressive mode\" blocking option.\r\n\r\n## Design\r\nFigma link: class="markdown-body" data-turbolinks="false"><div class="markdown-body safe-html-box__Uwc6Al"><h2 dir="auto">Description</h2>
<p dir="auto">We have received complaints from users about having to click through cookie consent banners related to real-time bidding. We should offer a global setting (default OFF) in Shields which would:</p>
<ol dir="auto">
<li>Automatically deny all data sharing (like the option that's available in the Cliqz browser and can be verified using the <a href="https://chrome.google.com/webstore/detail/reconsent/djcdlbbfldmndgenehaifaiiahhhagfa" rel="nofollow">re:consent extension</a>) in first-party consent manager platforms which follow the <a href="https://github.com/InteractiveAdvertisingBureau/GDPR-Transparency-and-Consent-Framework/blob/master/TCFv2/TCF-Implementation-Guidelines.md">IAB protocol</a>.</li>
<li>Hide banners using the <a href="https://easylist-downloads.adblockplus.org/easylist-cookie.txt" rel="nofollow">Easylist-Cookie</a> cosmetic filters.</li>
</ol>
<p dir="auto">We could surface that setting the first time a user encounters a cookie banner via a notification.</p>
<p dir="auto">Alternatively, instead of a new global setting, we could tie this feature to the existing "aggressive mode" blocking option.</p>
<h2 dir="auto">Design</h2>
<p dir="auto">Figma link: <a href="https://www.figma.com/file/cL22PpqneTYxJePORxUBKz/Cookie-consent-blocker?node-id=61%3A16268"
